articles.title: PDF to Text in Your Browser: pdf-lib Can't Extract Text, but pdf.js Can
articles.excerpt: If you want the words out of a PDF without uploading the file anywhere, the answer is one function: page.getTextContent() from Mozilla's pdf.js. And if you already build PDF tools with pdf-lib — the l…
articles.body: If you want the words out of a PDF without uploading the file anywhere, the answer is one function: page.getTextContent() from Mozilla's pdf.js. And if you already build PDF tools with pdf-lib — the library from my merging post — here is the thing nobody tells you until you waste an afternoon on it: pdf-lib cannot extract text at all. Both "do PDFs in JavaScript", but they do opposite halves of the job, and picking the wrong one is the most common dead end in browser PDF work. Below: what pdf.js does, the exact code already running in one of my production tools, and a real test on two real PDFs. The trap: pdf-lib is the wrong library for this job My PDF merger runs on pdf-lib, so when I needed text out of a PDF, I reached for the same library first.
articles.author: Shayan Ali

articles.title: fm-cli is in the official Omarchy package repo
articles.excerpt: I have been waiting on this one. fm-cli, my little terminal client for Fastmail, is now an optional package in the official Omarchy repo. It is not on the default install, which is fine: it is there i…
articles.body: I have been waiting on this one. fm-cli, my little terminal client for Fastmail, is now an optional package in the official Omarchy repo. It is not on the default install, which is fine: it is there if you want it, and it is not in anyone's way if you don't. On Omarchy, open the menu with Super + Space, choose Install > Package, and type fm-cli. Or, from a terminal: omarchy pkg add fm-cli Then sign in with fm-cli auth login , which opens Fastmail's consent page in your browser. That is it. fm-cli is a small Go client for Fastmail's JMAP API. It gives you a full-screen mail app in the terminal, commands that print JSON, a live watch over Fastmail's push connection, and offline reading and drafting. It is also the engine behind the Fastmail plugin for Omarchy .

articles.title: We built a 60 FPS JS + WebAssembly crackme to test if code protection has to lag (Syferit v2.1)
articles.excerpt: If you have ever tried running a heavy JavaScript obfuscator on a real production app, you already know the two usual outcomes: Your Next.js or Vite build either takes 25 minutes or crashes with a V8…
articles.body: If you have ever tried running a heavy JavaScript obfuscator on a real production app, you already know the two usual outcomes: Your Next.js or Vite build either takes 25 minutes or crashes with a V8 Out-Of-Memory error on third-party vendor chunks. Frame rates and Core Web Vitals tank because the runtime wrapper adds milliseconds to every hot function call. And on top of that, traditional variable renaming ( a , _0x1f2a ) barely slows down modern reverse-engineering workflows anymore. Frontier LLMs paired with AST analyzers, decompilers (Ghidra, WABT, ILSpy), and SMT solvers like Z3 reconstruct clean-room source code from minified bundles in minutes. Over the past few months at Soltrix Studios, we built Syferit , an open-core, 100% offline build-time code defense engine.
articles.author: Soltrix Studios

articles.title: Run Local Audio Stem Separation with Stem Separator and Docker
articles.excerpt: If you want to remove vocals from a song, isolate drums, or export several instrument tracks, sending audio to a third-party API is not your only option. Stem Separator is an open-source, self-hosted…
articles.body: If you want to remove vocals from a song, isolate drums, or export several instrument tracks, sending audio to a third-party API is not your only option. Stem Separator is an open-source, self-hosted web application that runs the separation pipeline on your own machine, homelab, or NAS. This tutorial uses the project's stable v1.0.0 release and Docker Compose. You will start the CPU version, verify its health endpoint, upload a supported audio file through the browser, and understand when the NVIDIA GPU configuration is appropriate. TL;DR Clone the repository, start the default Compose service, open http://localhost:7860 , and upload an MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A, AAC, OGG, or OPUS file. The default mode separates vocals and music.
articles.author: Fernando Paladini

articles.title: Giving a coding agent test results it can act on: JUnit XML, go test -json and a short failure summary
articles.excerpt: Most coding agents spend a large share of their turns in one loop: change code, run the tests, read the result, change code again. The quality of that loop depends on what "read the result" means. An…
articles.body: Most coding agents spend a large share of their turns in one loop: change code, run the tests, read the result, change code again. The quality of that loop depends on what "read the result" means. An exit code of 1 tells the model something failed and nothing about what. The full log tells it everything, at a cost in tokens and attention, and the one assertion that matters is somewhere in the middle. Test runners already know the answer in structured form. Most can write a report that lists every test, its status, and for each failure a message and a stack trace. This post shows how to get those reports out of a sandbox and turn them into a tool result built for a model: the counts, the first few failures, and a clear signal when the run did not finish at all.

articles.body: In some ways, the best found-footage movie ever made is still The Blair Witch Project . This wasn’t because of the film’s actual quality, but because of the effect it had on audiences back in 1999. When it was released, found-footage movies just weren't a well-known thing and the marketing campaign for the movie made it seem as though the events depicted actually happened. SPAC appears to closely follow Apple’s Private Cloud Compute blueprint, and the code references AI models like Google’s Gemma 4 and Alibaba’s Qwen 3.6. articles.title: Cosmic 'betta fish' glows in spectacular nebula portrait | Space photo of the day for Nov. 26, 2026
articles.excerpt: The striking blue of the Betta Fish Nebula swims across the cosmic landscape in a new image from the Dark Energy Camera.
articles.body: An image captured by the Dark Energy Camera showcasing the Betta Fish Nebula. (Image credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA) The striking blue of the Betta Fish Nebula swims across the cosmic landscape, a stunning wisp of material leftover from a stellar explosion. What is it? Roughly 6,800 light-years from Earth and nestled in the Centaurus constellation, this piece of the supernova remnant SNR G295.5+09.7 has earned the nickname the Betta Fish Nebula for its floaty, fishy shape. This almost ghostly whirl of gas and dust was created when a star much more massive than our sun exploded, blasting its outer layers of material outward in the process. Over time, the remnants of this supernova eruption stretched outward into space, dispersing and colliding with surrounding gas.

articles.body: The astronauts on the International Space Station will celebrate Thanksgiving with some nontraditional fare. Well, NASA astronaut Anil Menon will, anyway. In a video the agency released on Monday (Nov. 23), Menon showed off some of the plants he and his crewmates are growing in orbit and told us what's in store for the greens. "We need plants to survive as we set up our moon base , and as we go to Mars , we're going to have to grow our own nutrition. So that's what we're doing this Thanksgiving," Menon said in the 2.5-minute video. Astronauts deliver a Thanksgiving message from the International Space Station in November 2026. From left: NASA's Luke Delaney and Anil Menon, the Canadian Space Agency's Joshua Kutryk and NASA's Jessica Watkins.
